coverage.target: The Jenkins Build Site stage runs the same `npx astro build` that `just site-build` runs, and U3's Astro integration writes `_redirects.json` from the build-done hook's own output directory after checking every rule's grammar and target page, so the nightly build and the local build produce the same table with no separate pipeline step and no lifecycle hook.

The static server service `dev.rvnnt.blog` (`site/scripts/local-server.mjs`): one `stat` of the table and one map lookup per request, the table read only when its presence or modification time changes, and no file read for a redirect target, so the deploy's table placement is picked up live without a restart.

No infrastructure change: U3 adds no asset, process or pipeline stage, and the tunnel and the origin are unchanged. The Core Web Vitals budgets (LCP 2500 ms, CLS 0.1, TBT 200 ms) are measured on the built tree by the Build and Test stage.

The deployed artefact set gains one new non-page file - `_redirects.json` at the web root - and moves three page trees (`/tags` to `/writing/tags`, `/tags/<tag>` to `/writing/tags/<tag>`, `/graph` to `/writing/graph`); the Deploy stage and `just deploy` place it with a second copy after the tree, and the file-count check compares the page trees as moved, not as added files. The isolated-build budget is measured by the Build and Test stage.

No infrastructure change: U3 adds no logical request and renames no hashed asset - `grouped.css` is inlined into the pages that load it and no `_astro` bundle carries it; the inline growth and the 4096-byte guard are measured on the built tree by the Build and Test stage (`monitoring-design.md` Metrics, inline stylesheet budget).

The static server service writes the 301 itself, with `Cache-Control: no-cache`, from the rule's `to` percent-encoded exactly once with the request's raw query appended byte-for-byte; on a match a query carrying an encoded control byte is answered 400, a value the HTTP layer refuses is answered 400, and the handler never throws, so the launchd service stays up.

The static server gains the clean-URL rewrite's directory-index branch (BR3.6), the writer fails the build on a missing target page, and the Deploy stage and `just deploy` copy the tree first and the table second (`rsync --exclude=/_redirects.json`, then the table renamed into place), so a new rule never goes live before its page; the reverse residual - a removed tag's old rule live between the two copies - ends on the same 404 contract C5 promises.

The static server service accepts the table only in C4's shape and validates every rule's `from` and `to` against the acceptance grammar G1-G8; a table that fails any condition is rejected whole, with one error line to the launchd log and no redirect. The writer runs the same grammar and fails the build first, so the nightly table cannot be one the server rejects.

Every redirect target is the table's own decoded absolute path - the acceptance grammar admits no scheme, no authority and no percent-escape - so the 301 names only a path on the site's own origin; the containment check still guards every file the server serves, including the table and a directory's `index.html`.

One origin: the Cloudflare Tunnel `obsidian-blog` publishes the static server through `http://127.0.0.1:8080`, while the launchd agent binds `0.0.0.0:8080`, so the same origin is also reachable on the LAN (recorded and accepted in `infrastructure-specification.md` > Networking topology: everything it serves is already public). The moved pages load nothing from another origin, the graph data file stays at the site's own root, and the table is served as `application/json` from that same root.
No infrastructure change: the JavaScript-off check runs in the local crossunit browser project over the built tree; U3 adds no island and no runtime dependency.

No infrastructure change: the axe matrix runs in the local HIG browser project against the built site. U3 changes one manual-review-subject file - `site/astro.config.mjs` - so the 16-state manual record is invalidated and `npm run test:e2e` fails closed until the maintainer redoes that review once, before the nightly deploy that ships U3's moved pages.

The Jenkins Verify stage runs `cargo test --release`, `npm run test:unit` and `npm run test:pbt` before Deploy, and `cicd-pipeline.md` lists every test file that carries an old-address expectation (five HIG specs and `support/hig.ts`, updated; two unit/property files, confirmed), so the recorded Construction Verification Command stays green on every change that ships.

The HIG harness (`site/scripts/hig/build-and-serve.mjs`) serves the built `site/dist` through the production server on 127.0.0.1:4329, so the redirect criteria are proved at HTTP level against the code launchd runs; the dotted key is proved by a Vitest check that runs the same server as a child on a free port (never 8080 or 4329) over a temporary web root, inside the Jenkins Verify stage.
